I am thinking about how to farm this year. My land is only 5 mu, so I cannot afford a bad harvest. Last two years I followed what my uncle and neighbors do, and it worked okay, so I will do mostly the same.

For wheat, I plant in October after maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the town dealer — the bag he sells most. I use about 40 kg per mu of seed, maybe a little more because I broadcast and it is not so even. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about two bags (100 kg) for the 5 mu, so 20 kg per mu. That gives roughly 3 kg of N, 3 kg P, 3 kg K from the base. Then at spring green-up I top-dress urea, one bag (50 kg) for whole field, plus another half bag around jointing. Urea is 46 percent N, so this gives me maybe 20 kg N more per mu. Total N near 23 kg. I would rather put a little extra than see yellow leaves — bad wheat is a disaster, one bag of urea is only 100 yuan. I water at green-up, at jointing, and at grain-filling if dry. Three times usually. I plow with the tractor man from the village — he charges by mu. Pesticide I spray twice, once for aphids and once mixed with herbicide. My neighbors get around 450 kg per mu, I hope for the same.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no-till with the seeder, hybrid seed — Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has that year, everyone plants it. One bag of compound fertilizer as base, 20 kg per mu, then top-dress urea at big trumpet stage, one full bag across the field plus some more, about 18 kg N per mu added. Maize needs water in summer but rain usually comes; I irrigate maybe twice if July is dry. Spray once for borer, maybe a second time if I see worms. My neighbors get 550 kg per mu, that is my target.
